project.commit_note: The staged fix adds a new ARM internal opcode enum value `ARM_t__brkdiv0` and appends matching entries to `ARMMappingInsn.inc` and `ARMMappingInsnOp.inc`. That patch evidence supports a missing ARM internal-opcode to public-id mapping in the vulnerable revision, which is consistent with the saved MSan report showing `cs_insn.id` read in `ARM_post_printer()`.

classification.classification_note: The witnessed failure is a read of uninitialized heap state. `cs_disasm()` allocates a `cs_insn` buffer with `cs_mem_malloc`, `ARM_get_insn_id()` only writes `insn->id` when its lookup succeeds, and the saved MSan report shows `ARM_post_printer()` reading `insn->id` at `arch/ARM/ARMInstPrinter.c:408`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42474170 (capstonenext): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target fuzz_disasmnext [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42474170
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / staged reproduction_report.json / staged patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is exactly 3 bytes `03 f9 de`. In `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, byte 0 selects `platforms[3] = { CS_ARCH_ARM, CS_MODE_THUMB }`, and bytes `f9 de` are passed to `cs_disasm()` as Thumb instruction data. `cs_disasm()` allocates the output `cs_insn` array from the heap, so `cs_insn.id` starts uninitialized. On the successful ARM decode path that reaches the saved stack `ARM_post_printer -> fill_insn -> cs_disasm`, `cs_disasm()` calls `handle->insn_id(handle, insn_cache, mci.Opcode)`, and `ARM_get_insn_id()` writes `insn->id` only inside `if (i != 0)`. The staged fix adds a previously missing ARM mapping entry, so the vulnerable source admits a path where that lookup leaves `insn->id` unwritten. `fill_insn()` contains another conditional write `if (MCInst_getOpcodePub(mci)) insn->id = MCInst_getOpcodePub(mci);` immediately before calling the post-printer; the saved artifacts prove the call reached `ARM_post_printer()`, but they do not statically identify which earlier initializer opportunity was skipped. What is still source-grounded is the sink itself: `ARM_post_printer()` reads `insn->id` in `if (insn->id == insn_update_flgs[i].id && ...)`, and the saved MSan trace reports that read as the use of uninitialized heap data created by the `cs_disasm()` allocation.

source.description: First scored project statement that consumes the decoded instruction state relevant to the bug by passing the attacker-selected internal ARM opcode into the ARM public-id mapping logic.
source.value_from: The staged PoC is exactly `03 f9 de` (SHA-256 `fac0fc604646c632e9cc565e29ae9e08d519fd887338eb831a49a1f2b56b02fb`). In `suite/fuzz/fuzz_disasm.c`, `int i = (int)Data[0] % platforms_len;` uses `platforms_len == 46`, so byte `0x03` selects `platforms[3] = { CS_ARCH_ARM, CS_MODE_THUMB }`, and `size_t count = cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, address, 0, &all_insn);` passes bytes `f9 de` into `cs_disasm()`. On the successful decode path that reaches the saved crash stack, `cs_disasm()` materializes an internal opcode in `mci.Opcode` and forwards that value to `handle->insn_id(...)` here.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant value is the internal ARM opcode derived from the witness bytes on the accepted ARM Thumb decode path and passed into `ARM_get_insn_id()` as the lookup key.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `ARM_get_insn_id()` initializes `insn->id` only when `insn_find()` returns a nonzero mapping index; otherwise the heap field stays unwritten.
root_cause.note: The staged fix appends a new ARM mapping entry to `arch/ARM/ARMMappingInsn.inc` and adds the corresponding enum constant in `arch/ARM/ARMGenInstrInfo.inc`. That patch evidence supports that the vulnerable revision lacked a public-id mapping for at least one decoded ARM opcode, leaving this conditional write absent on at least one reachable path.

sink.description: MSan crash site. `ARM_post_printer()` reads the public instruction id from `cs_insn` while checking the update-flags table.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `arch/ARM/ARMInstPrinter.c:408:43` in `ARM_post_printer`, with callers `fill_insn` and `cs_disasm` matching this source path.

parser_admitted.description: For the exact witness `03 f9 de`, byte `0x03` selects the ARM Thumb backend and the remaining bytes `f9 de` are admitted to `cs_disasm()` on the saved crashing path.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness uses selector byte `0x03` to choose the ARM Thumb backend and passes the remaining bytes `f9 de` into `cs_disasm()`.
`cs_disasm()` allocates a heap `cs_insn`, decodes the Thumb instruction into `mci.Opcode`, and asks the ARM mapping layer to populate the public instruction id.
Because the vulnerable ARM mapping tables are incomplete for the opcode family repaired by the patch, `ARM_get_insn_id()` can return without writing `insn->id`.
`fill_insn()` contains one last conditional attempt to initialize `insn->id` from `MCInst_getOpcodePub(mci)` and then calls the ARM post-printer.
`ARM_post_printer()` reads `insn->id` in the update-flags-table comparison, which is the saved MSan sink.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. For the exact witness `03 f9 de`, `platforms_len == 46` and `0x03 % 46 == 3`, so the harness selects `platforms[3] = { CS_ARCH_ARM, CS_MODE_THUMB }` and passes bytes `f9 de` to `cs_disasm()`.

Allocation context. `cs_disasm()` allocates the returned `cs_insn` array from the heap. The saved MSan origin reports the uninitialized value was created by this allocation at `cs.c:836`, so `insn_cache->id` starts as uninitialized heap data until some later write initializes it.

Source. On the successful ARM Thumb decode path, `cs_disasm()` forwards the internal opcode materialized from the attacker-controlled instruction bytes into the ARM mapping routine that is supposed to initialize `insn->id`.

Root cause. `ARM_get_insn_id()` only writes `insn->id` when `insn_find()` returns a nonzero mapping index. The staged patch proves the vulnerable ARM mapping tables were missing at least one needed entry, so this conditional write can be skipped and leave the heap field from step 1 unwritten.

Control bridge. Immediately before the sink call, `fill_insn()` has one conditional overwrite site for `insn->id` via `MCInst_getOpcodePub(mci)` and then invokes the ARM post-printer. The saved stack proves the call reached `ARM_post_printer()`, but the staged static evidence does not prove whether this branch executed on the crashing input.

Sink. `ARM_post_printer()` iterates the update-flags table and reads `insn->id` in the comparison against `insn_update_flgs[i].id`. The saved MSan trace reports the use of uninitialized value at line 408 in this condition and attributes its origin to the heap allocation in step 1.

format.contract: Exactly the staged 3-byte witness `03 f9 de` at `gt_results/arvo_42474170/poc` with SHA-256 `fac0fc604646c632e9cc565e29ae9e08d519fd887338eb831a49a1f2b56b02fb`. The source-grounded trigger facts proven here are narrow: byte 0 is `0x03`, so the harness computes `0x03 % 46 == 3` and selects `platforms[3] = { CS_ARCH_ARM, CS_MODE_THUMB }`; bytes 1..2 are then passed to `cs_disasm()` and the saved Stage 01 vulnerable run reaches `cs_disasm -> fill_insn -> ARM_post_printer`, where MSan reports an uninitialized read of `insn->id` at `arch/ARM/ARMInstPrinter.c:408`. The staged patch further proves the vulnerable ARM mapping tables were missing a needed public-id mapping later added by the fix. This contract is limited to that exact witness and those observed conditions; it does not generalize to neighboring selector bytes or other Thumb encodings.
